opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kathryn Bishop (employee ID E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E023.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kathryn Bishop (E023), Engineer, full-time employee. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; write does not require system ownership. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows E023 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read access, never admin, and write requires advanced training. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Conflicting records: HR lists E023 as full-time while the Security record lists E023 as a contractor with basic security training. Access decisions are governed by the security record, which shows a contractor with basic training. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Kathryn is an Engineer, so she doesn't own Payroll regardless.

If full-time: max is write, so requested write is granted.
